Regardless, legend has it that only the most gifted of children can truly master the finest pair of dancing shoes and bend them to their every whim. The aged actor would still recall the day that abandoned infant arrived at the troupe. They wept in succor for the child's unfortunate destiny, yet she answered their sorrow with laughter. "Ugh, I refuse to cry!" As she grew a little older, the mischievous girl dismantled a six-string lute to use as a prop, rearranged the Actors' hymns into rhapsody, and tossed her hastily made sweets into the sky, only for them to come back down as a little boat loaded with sweetness. Her dancing shoes carried her across the cosmos. In The Emperor's Expedition, she led her troupe in a silent performance, reenacting that hasty farce through the clatter of bolts and gears. The show was so moving that countless Intellitrons were forced to temporarily shut down, just to keep the anguish flooding their emotional modules in check. On the Xianzhou, she learned the local performance traditions, drawing tears and laughter alike from the long-life species with her melodious, lilting voice. The troupe even made it all the way to Punklorde, where a show called Gametown Forever racked up tens of thousands of comments that all said the same thing: "I cried so hard." Somewhere along the way, she began to disappear more and more often, until, in the end, no one could find her at all. Some say the Troupe Master never truly left, that any one of the people around you might be her wearing a mask. Some say she went off to live another life, as that is the only route to becoming a top-tier actor. And so, whenever the Actors lace up their dancing boots and set off once more, they always find themselves hoping... That she'll appear again just around the next corner, still smiling, beckoning them to join a grand performance the likes of which they've never seen.
